text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Friday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- New financial accounting forms come into force January 1, 1997 and business people are queuing to buy the expensive documents since otherwise business transactions will not be possible.
- Parliament passed Thursday the basic national security law which was under consideration for five years.
- Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius criticised the present privatisation system which allows people to manipulate but not to privatise.

- Bank of Lithuania registered 42 million litas share capital of Ukio Bank and allowed Nomura International to acquire 33.3 percent of it. Now 55 percent of share capital of the bank will be in the hands of foreign investors.
- The new government does not intend to reopen the problem-hit Innovation Bank, which was closed one year ago.
- The best basketball player of Europe in 1996, Arturas Karnisovas, who plays for Barcelona, was decorated by President Brazauskas.

- All the banks in Lithuania have gathered the required 20 million litas share capital, the Bank of Lithuania said. The bank registered the 67 million litas share capital of Hermis Bank, boosted by 24.6 million litas and Ukio Bank's 42 million litas share capital, which grew by 18 million litas.
- Privatisation should be revised and companies should be sold in open tenders, Vagnorius told a press conference.
- The government plans a 697.8 million litas budget deficit for 1997 and will not increase state debt.
- 31 percent of petroleum in Lithuania was smuggled in in 1995.
- Pepsi Cola General Bottlers will sign a contract to produce beverages in Lithuania in 1997 and intends to invest several million dollars.
